🔁 **Nothing borrowed any more:** the 2 Pit Rookie, 1 Punch First and 1 Graves this list used to borrow came from your Ambessa deck, which you took apart on Nov 21, so they live in Fiora for good.

### 🧳 Sideboard

Sideboard (10): 3 Decree of Unity, 2 Bonds of Strength (your 3rd is spare since Ambessa was taken apart), 3 Strike Down, 1 Riposte and 2 Show of Strength. Retested Nov 20 with 1,500 games per matchup.

- **Vs Ziggs (54% → 58%):** in 3 Decree of Unity; out 2 Riposte, 1 Ki Barrier (the old Strike Down slots). Ziggs's key units are Chaos.
- **Vs Kai'Sa and Ambessa (Kai'Sa 48% → 51%, Ambessa 21% → 24%):** in 2 Bonds of Strength; out 2 Ki Barrier (the old Strike Down slots).
- **Vs everything else:** keep the main deck. Decree of Unity was even against Kennen and 1–4 points worse against Zed and Vex. Bonds of Strength lost 2–5 points against Ziggs, K'Sante, Jarvan and Orianna, so only bring it in for the two matchups above. Lacerate lost 4–7 points in earlier tests, so it's out of the sideboard.

### 🎮 How to play

Game plan: make units Mighty (5+ Might) to ramp with your legend and ready them with Fiora, Worthy.

💡 Tips:

- Put equipment on units that are hard to remove.
- Hold Ki Barrier for the fight that matters: it stops the next 7 damage, so the unit carrying your B.F. Sword survives a fight it was going to win.
- Riposte counters any spell, not only ones aimed at your units: removal, sweepers, pumps, even draw spells. Keep 2 Energy and 2 Power open on turns the opponent is likely to cast something big; the unit you choose also gets + Might equal to that spell's cost.
- Graves, Blasting Through deals his Might to every enemy unit there when he attacks or defends, but deals no combat damage himself. Equip him: a Mighty Graves wipes small units before the fight starts.
- In long games, spread equipment across units and keep 1–2 cards in hand to rebuild after removal.
- Fiora, Victorious gets Deflect, Ganking and Shield once she's Mighty: equip her early so she's hard to remove and can move between battlefields.

⚡ Combos:

- K'Sante, Courageous defends at 6 Might with Shield 2, so he becomes Mighty: your legend channels a rune and Fiora, Worthy can ready him. Holding a battlefield with him channels another rune toward your Rift Heralds.
- Rift Herald: when it moves to a battlefield, draw a unit from your top 3. When it dies, play a unit from your hand for free, so try to hold a K'Sante.
- Punch First or B.F. Sword to win the fight, then Ki Barrier to keep the winner alive.
- Riposte a removal spell aimed at your B.F. Sword carrier: the spell is countered and the unit gets + Might equal to its cost, often enough to win the fight it was in.
- Boneshiver on Lucian, Merciless: when he conquers, you channel an extra rune and he readies to attack again.

### 🧳 Sideboard

Sideboard (10): 3 Renekton, Rage Fueled, 3 Existential Dread, 2 Zed, Without a Sound (all from your old Zed deck) and 2 Siren's Song. Built around your Nov 20 list and tested with 700 games per matchup.

- **Games 2 and 3 against everything except Vex: in 3 Renekton, Rage Fueled, 3 Existential Dread and 2 Zed, Without a Sound; out 2 Brittle Steel, 3 Tideturner, 2 Hexplosive Minefield and 1 Lingering Animus.** It won more in every matchup, about 11 points on average: Kai'Sa 41% → 58%, Kennen 77% → 86%, Master Yi 50% → 58%, Ambessa 21% → 34%, Fiora 35% → 50%, K'Sante 56% → 63%, Jarvan 49% → 63%, Orianna 64% → 77%.
- **Vs Vex: in 2 Siren's Song; out 2 Brittle Steel** (79% → 84%). The big swap above was only about 1 point better against Vex.
- **If you'd rather keep Tideturner:** bring in 3 Renekton and 3 Existential Dread for 2 Brittle Steel, 2 Lingering Animus and 2 Hexplosive Minefield instead. That was about 9 points better on average, close to the swap above.
- Your Nov 20 list tested about 8 points below the list it replaced (53% vs 61% in the same 9 matchups). Brittle Steel was the weakest card (the deck did better with a blank card in its place) and Tideturner was even with a blank, which is why both go out first.

### 🎮 How to play

Game plan: place Bombs, set them off with your own effects, and hold battlefields.

💡 Tips:

- Place a Bomb with your legend on turn 2.
- Each Bomb deals 2 to one enemy unit there (3 with Ziggs, Short-Fused), and when one dies all your other Bombs at that battlefield go off too. Stack Bombs where you want to pick off several small units.
- Damage heals at the end of every fight and every turn, so ping with Akali or set off Bombs right before you attack, not after.
- When Ziggs, Explosive defends, kill a Bomb there for +2 Might: the Bombs hit the attackers too.
- When you kill a gear, pick a Bomb for damage, or Gold if that doesn't matter.
- Any deck can hide Hidden cards: pay 1 Power to put Switcheroo face down at a battlefield you control. From your next turn you can play it there for free as a Reaction, even in the middle of their attack.

⚡ Combos:

- Tideturner + Akali, Deadly Weapon: when you play Tideturner it swaps places with a friendly unit, and that counts as a move, so Akali deals 1 (2 if Empowered) to a unit at the battlefield she moved to or from. Hide Tideturner at a battlefield, then flip it mid-fight to pull Akali in and ping a blocker.
- Switcheroo flipped mid-fight swaps their biggest attacker's Might with your smallest unit's.
- Hexplosive Minefield: kill all your Bombs at once (each deals 2), and at the end of the turn you get the same number of Bombs back.
- Ziggs, Short-Fused: every hit from your gear deals 1 more.
- Riven readies Ziggs, Explosive after he makes a Bomb, so he makes a second one.
- Exhaust Reckless Innovator for Riven's ability: you get Gold or a card, and Ziggs readies.
- Any gear dying lets Lingering Animus enter ready.

📈 **Best opening lines** (from 4,000 simulated games against your decks and the meta; turn 1 = your first turn):

- **Go first if you can:** Ziggs wins 67% going first and 53% going second.
- **Turn 1:** Ziggs, Explosive (65%), Amateur Demolitionist (63%) or Lingering Animus (62%).
- **Turn 2:** Ziggs, Explosive (65%, the most common play); Akali, Deadly Weapon 62%.
- **Turn 3:** hide Switcheroo (72%), Explosimian (68%) or Ziggs, Short-Fused (66%).
- These come from 6,000 games with the right-now list after the trick-play upgrade.

Sideboard (10): 3 Decree of Focus, 2 Hush, 3 Twilight Shroud, 1 Hunting Blind, 1 Punch First (all cards you own). Retested Nov 20 with 2,000 games per matchup.

Game plan: stack Shield on one unit, double it, attack with it, and use Ntofo Strikes to win the key fight; Discipline keeps your hand full. Hold your spells for fights and your opponent's turn rather than spending them in your main phase: the self-learning AI found this is worth about 5 points in almost every K'Sante matchup (Discipline, Show of Strength and Life from Stone are all Reactions).

- Keep K'Sante, Dauntless at the same battlefield as your stacked unit; he only doubles units there.
- Ramp with Life from Stone, K'Sante, Courageous and Ruined Monastery to cast Rostrum around turn 6.
- Once your rune deck is empty, holding Cosmic Vista scores an extra point. Twilight Shroud is a sideboard card: bring it in against decks with a lot of damage-based removal.

⚡ Combos:

- Staunch Survivor + Nazuman Ntofo (Shield 4), doubled by Dauntless (Shield 8), then your legend (1 Energy, one unit per turn): +8 Might on the attack.
- Ntofo Strikes after doubling deals damage equal to the unit's Shield. It's an Action, so you can also cast it mid-fight, even while defending on their turn.
- Graves + Nazuman Ntofo + your legend: he attacks at 6 Might and deals 6 to every enemy there.
- Wrath of the Freljord enters ready with 7 Might and Shield 3, so it can attack the turn you play it.
- Rostrum: exhaust it to draw, channel a rune, and give a unit +3 Might.
- Irresistible Faefolk: move it to Graves' battlefield to drag an extra enemy into his damage, or pull their best unit onto your stacked Shield unit.

📈 **Best opening lines** (from 4,000 simulated games against your decks and the meta; turn 1 = your first turn):

- **Go first if you can:** K'Sante wins 61% going first and 41% going second.
- **Turn 1:** Pit Rookie (57%) is best; Staunch Survivor (52%) is the most common.
- **Turn 2:** K'Sante, Dauntless or Graves (55%), Serene Ascetic (54%). Ntofo Strikes on turn 2 won only 43%: hold it for a fight.
- **Turn 3:** Graves (65%), then Nazuman Ntofo, Pit Rookie or K'Sante, Courageous (55%).

## 🏰 Jarvan IV (Body / Order)

Legend: Jarvan IV, Exemplar of Demacia. Chosen Champion: Jarvan IV, Martial Paragon. Runes: 7 Body, 5 Order. Battlefields: Seat of Power, Black Market, Hunters' Circle.

**New deck, built to replace Seraphine.** It uses Seraphine's Trifarian Captains, Hunting Dogs and Burn Away, your Radiance and Vendetta cards, and a few cards you swap in from other decks. On Nov 19 it was re-optimised with your full collection (Armored Tusker, Sandshifter, a 3rd Royal Heir and a 3rd Hunting Dog), and 3 Demacian Standards stay in at your call. With Martial Paragon out, a Standard can be played mid-fight for a surprise +2 and an extra unit. On Nov 20 the 4-card swap from the sideboard (Masa, Leona, Combat Chef and Dauntless Vanguard) moved into the main deck because it tested 1–2 points better in every matchup. In the AI 3.1 tests (Nov 21) this list wins 38% against your decks and 48% against the LA meta decks (Rengar, Vex, Master Yi). Black Market and Hunters' Circle tested slightly better than Monastery of Hirana and Sunken Temple, so you don't need to order those. In real tournaments Jarvan hasn't proven himself yet: 17 Jarvan players at the Sacramento Showdown went 51-63-1, with a best finish of 76th.

### 🎮 How to play

Game plan: play cheap units, then play a Deploy gear (Pillaged Armory or Demacian Standard) to an empty battlefield and use your legend to move a unit there. That conquers right away, even with a unit you only just played.

💡 Tips:

- Your legend's move costs 1 rune of any colour and works once per round, because it exhausts the legend. Once Martial Paragon is out your Deploy gear can be played in showdowns, so you can save the move to pull a defender in on your opponent's turn.
- Demacian Standard returns to your hand when you hold its battlefield, so you can play it again next turn for another move and another +2 Might.
- With Martial Paragon out, you can drop a Standard in the middle of a fight on your turn and use your legend to move a unit in: +2 Might plus the extra unit. Keep 2 Energy and 2 Power open when you attack so the threat is real.
- Graves deals damage equal to his Might to every enemy in the fight, but no combat damage. Send him into battlefields with several small units.

⚡ Combos:

- Martial Paragon conquering a battlefield where you have a Deploy gear channels an extra rune.
- Seat of Power: conquer it while you already control the other battlefield to draw a card, so take the open battlefield first.
- Jarvan IV, Royal Heir pulls another of your units into his fight when he attacks.

📈 **Best opening lines** (from 4,000 simulated games with the 3-Standard list against your decks and the meta; turn 1 = your first turn):

- **Go first if you can:** Jarvan wins 59% going first and 45% going second.
- **Turn 1:** a unit, not gear: Disciple of Shen (62%) is best, then Hunting Dog (54%). Demacian Standard on turn 1 won only 23%; save Standards until you have units to move.
- **Turn 2:** Graves when you can (64%), Pit Rookie or Leona, Determined (58%).
- **Turn 3:** Graves (66%), Legion Marauder or Hunting Dog (58%); start Deploying gear to empty battlefields.

- **Vs Kai'Sa, Ziggs and Zed (Kai'Sa 33% → 48%, Ziggs 24% → 31%, Zed 66% → 72%):** in 3 Decree of Focus; out 2 Esteemed Hierophant (they took the Improvised Projectile slots), 1 Scrutinizing Scope. All three are Fury decks. (Cutting Invigorating Bloom instead tested worse.)

### 🎮 How to play

Game plan: play expensive gear, then bring it to life with your legend and fight with it.

- Move or attack with Strigian Oracle each turn: every time it exhausts, check your top card and send it to the bottom if it isn't gear you need.

⚡ Combos:

- Animate The Ball: a 5-Might unit with Ganking that draws or deals 2 every time it moves. Deploy it first, then choose it with your legend at the start of your next main phase. Your legend can pick a gear at a battlefield, not only in your base. Becoming a unit isn't a move (no draw or 2 damage then). If the Ball sits at a battlefield your opponent left empty, animating it contests it right away and you conquer it; if their units are there, it starts a fight with the Ball attacking, so only do it when 5 Might wins.
- Spirit of the Forge returns The Ball to your hand so you can replay it for its trigger.
- Battle Preparations showing off a gear readies 2 runes, helping you cast Rostrum sooner.
- Command: Attack finds a gear from your top 5 cards, or moves a Deploy gear like The Ball.
- Life from Stone, exhausting Strigian Oracle to pay for it: draw 1, gain a rune, and Oracle Predicts, all for 1 energy.
- Invigorating Bloom + animated Rostrum: exhaust Rostrum to draw 1, and Rostrum's own trigger gives a unit +3 Might. Do this on turns you are holding, not attacking.
